PullRequest.Title: terminal: stop run_in_terminal sending Ctrl+U into PowerShell commands (fixes flake)
PullRequest.Body:

**TL;DR:** `chat - run_in_terminal › no-output command reports empty output` flaked on Windows with `cmd: The term 'cmd' is not recognized…`. When shell integration comes up a few ms after the 5 s wait, `run_in_terminal` falls back to its `none` strategy, which types Ctrl+U before the command. PowerShell's PSReadLine (default Windows edit mode) has no Ctrl+U binding and inserts the raw `\x15`, so `cmd /c rem` ran as `\x15cmd /c rem`. This is a product bug, not a test bug: the fix stops treating shell *output* as pending user input and never sends Ctrl+U to PowerShell on Windows.

### CI failures
- ADO `main` build [485970](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=485970&view=results), 2026-10-19, Windows X64, `Run integration tests (Electron)`. It was the only failure in 436 Windows Electron integration runs on `main` from 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-20. None of the 152 failed `Windows / Electron` jobs of `pr.yml` in that window hit it.

### Root cause
From the failing build's `terminal.log` and `exthost.log`:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 31.917 | First terminal of the window (pty host just spawned). `ToolTerminalCreator` waits 5000 ms for shell integration ([toolTerminalCreator.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c3890577dad36cbeabe43583c12262be20b77cca/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/toolTerminalCreator.ts#L94)) |
| 36.918 | Wait times out, so the tool uses the `none` execute strategy |
| 36.992 | Shell integration activates, 74 ms late (`terminal-suggest` activated on `onTerminalShellIntegration:*`) |
| ~38 | `none` strategy sends `\x15`, then `cmd /c rem\r` |
| 39.024 | Command fails (`npm` activated on `onTerminalQuickFixRequest`) |
| 40.025 | Tool result: `cmd: The term 'cmd' is not recognized…` |

Two defects combine:
1. `_registerInputListener` sets `receivedUserInput` from `instance.onData` ([runInTerminalTool.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c3890577dad36cbeabe43583c12262be20b77cca/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/runInTerminalTool.ts#L2770)). That event is *"the raw data stream coming from the pty"* ([terminal.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c3890577dad36cbeabe43583c12262be20b77cca/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminal.ts#L1053)), so a shell printing its prompt counts as user input.
2. With that flag set, the `none` and `basic` strategies send Ctrl+U to clear pending input ([noneExecuteStrategy.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c3890577dad36cbeabe43583c12262be20b77cca/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/noneExecuteStrategy.ts#L84), [basicExecuteStrategy.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/c3890577dad36cbeabe43583c12262be20b77cca/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/basicExecuteStrategy.ts#L207)). On Windows, PSReadLine defaults to its Windows edit mode ([Cmdlets.cs](https://github.com/PowerShell/PSReadLine/blob/a2d143f78904f8a954f8d4b055e55ceca6939bfc/PSReadLine/Cmdlets.cs#L177)), which doesn't bind Ctrl+U ([KeyBindings.cs](https://github.com/PowerShell/PSReadLine/blob/a2d143f78904f8a954f8d4b055e55ceca6939bfc/PSReadLine/KeyBindings.cs#L177)). Unbound keys are self-inserted ([ReadLine.cs](https://github.com/PowerShell/PSReadLine/blob/a2d143f78904f8a954f8d4b055e55ceca6939bfc/PSReadLine/ReadLine.cs#L707)). xterm.js doesn't render the inserted NAK, so the error looks like `cmd` is missing from PATH.

### Fix
- `_registerInputListener` now listens to `onDidInputData`, i.e. data written *to* the pty (keystrokes, terminal replies, the tool's own text). A fresh terminal no longer counts as having pending input.
- New `canClearPromptInputWithCtrlU()` in `strategyHelpers.ts`: the `none` and `basic` strategies don't send Ctrl+U to **PowerShell on Windows**, detected by the launch executable or the detected shell type. PSReadLine's Emacs edit mode, the default on macOS and Linux, binds Ctrl+U to `BackwardKillInput`, so pwsh there (and bash, zsh, fish everywhere) keeps Ctrl+U. On Windows, Ctrl+U never cleared pending input; it was inserted alongside it. No other key clears the line safely in every PSReadLine mode: Escape is a chord prefix in Emacs mode, and Ctrl+C accepts an empty line that shell integration reports as a finished command.
- `BasicExecuteStrategy` now interrupts a still-running command (Ctrl+C when `executingCommandObject` is set) independently of the pending-input flag. The old `onData` listener set that flag on any process output, so a process that kept running after the idle fallback used to be interrupted; without this, the next command would be typed into it.
- The integration test is unchanged and stays strict.

### Evidence
| Check | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| CI Windows, 30× loop of this test with the shell integration wait forced to time out (as on ADO) | ❌ [failed on attempt 1/30](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39510555890/job/118930213292) with the CI symptom `cmd: The term 'cmd' is not recognized…` | ✅ [30/30 passed](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39510668205/job/118930592836), all 30 through the `none` strategy (per the run's `terminal.log`) |
| Local pty, pwsh 7.6.7 / PSReadLine 2.4.5, `-EditMode Windows`, send `\x15true\r` | `The term '\x15true' is not recognized` | n/a (Ctrl+U no longer sent) |
| Same, send `true\r` (or `-EditMode Emacs` + `\x15true\r`) | runs | runs |
| New unit tests (`none`/`basic` strategies send no Ctrl+U to pwsh on Windows, Ctrl+C to a still-running command; shell output is not pending input) | 3/3 fail, e.g. pwsh on Windows gets `['\x15', 'cmd /c rem']` | 3/3 pass |

Stress PRs (temporary, closed): baseline #343069, with fix #343070 (run on the first commit; the review follow-up 44a2172413f keeps the Windows PowerShell path identical). They run only the `Windows / Electron` job and set `terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.timeout: 0` in the suite setup, so every attempt falls back to the `none` strategy as build 485970 did.

### Validation
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/noneExecuteStrategy.test.ts --run …/test/browser/basicExecuteStrategy.test.ts --run …/test/electron-browser/runInTerminalTool.test.ts --run …/test/browser/strategyHelpers.test.ts --run …/test/browser/richExecuteStrategy.test.ts --run …/test/browser/executeStrategy.test.ts`: 277 passing, 108 pending, 0 failing
- Same new tests with the product change reverted: they fail (as expected). Reverting only the running-command check fails the `*StillExecuting` scenarios.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: clean
- `npm run typecheck-client`: clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: clean

No UI changes.

cc @meganrogge

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal run_in_terminal command in a fresh or reused terminal using no/basic shell integration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Terminal initialization/reuse, xterm readiness, the existing idle wait, one PTY write for the command, then command completion/idle detection. The listener change is passive and does not add work before progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the requested command to the terminal PTY via ITerminalInstance.sendText
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command write per invocation, plus the pre-existing optional Ctrl+U write only when actual input is pending and the shell supports it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command write occurred, while any shell output could mark the prompt as having pending input and cause an unnecessary Ctrl+U PTY write plus a 100 ms idle wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested command write remains on the critical path; the diff does not increase normal-path boundary calls and avoids classifying high-volume shell output as pending input.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One listener callback per input write rather than per PTY output chunk; command count controls executions, with one cached foreground terminal per chat session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Foreground commands are serialized through one reused terminal; background commands use separate terminals. The changed strategy operations remain sequential and add no aggregate concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Foreground terminal association is reused warm per chat session; cold creation still performs the unchanged terminal/profile/shell-integration setup. No cache key, miss, or invalidation behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: terminalInstance shows onData is PTY output while onDidInputData fires after process writes from keyboard/tool input; strategy call flow and waits are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact output-event volume varies by command, but the changed listener strictly moves away from the potentially high-volume PTY output stream and does not increase normal command latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The listener reduces callback frequency for output-heavy commands and can remove unnecessary pre-command PTY writes/waits.

Scenarios.Scenario: run_in_terminal on Windows PowerShell with pending terminal input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing pre-execution idle wait, shell/OS detection now skips Ctrl+U and its following 100 ms idle wait, then sends the command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: PTY input writes for Ctrl+U and the requested command
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Changed from optional Ctrl+U plus command to command only for Windows PowerShell; one removed PTY write and one removed 100 ms idle wait per affected invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: When the pending-input flag was true, the strategy wrote Ctrl+U, waited for 100 ms of PTY idleness, then wrote the command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff shortens this path by removing the unsupported clearing write and wait.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One shell classification per command invocation; constant-size path/enum checks. Effective boundary cardinality drops from two PTY writes to one when pending input is recorded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations are serialized within the terminal strategy; no new task, queue, or parallel PTY activity is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Detection uses current terminal shell type, launch executable, and OS on each invocation with constant work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the helper result directly gates the existing sendText and waitForIdle calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency depends on Windows PowerShell use and pending-input state, but direction is definitively reduced work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. This is a bounded latency and boundary-call reduction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Basic shell integration reuses a terminal whose previous command remains active after idle fallback
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The strategy first waits for PTY idleness, observes executingCommandObject, writes Ctrl+C, waits for 100 ms of post-interrupt idleness, then writes the next command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send Ctrl+C through the terminal PTY before the next command
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly guaranteed interrupt write when command detection reports an active prior command; previously this happened only if the pending-input flag was also true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: If receivedUserInput was false, the strategy skipped the interrupt and immediately wrote the next command despite the active command object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one PTY write and a 100 ms idle interval on this recovery path before sending the next command, while preventing the next command from being written into the still-running process.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one added interrupt PTY write and one idle wait per new invocation while a prior command object is still executing; it does not scale with output history or collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The interrupt, idle wait, and next command are deliberately serialized. No burst or per-item parallelism exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The warm foreground terminal is reused; there is no result cache. Shell integration state is read directly from the existing command-detection capability.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added boundary and critical-path wait; high that it is limited to an already-running prior process and one operation per invocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: This recovery state is uncommon and exact process response time varies; the explicit idle duration is 100 ms after the last output.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is bounded, occurs only on a degraded recovery path, and is required to preserve command execution semantics rather than redundant scalable work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Lifetime of the terminal input listener on cached and disposed tool terminals
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The listener only updates a boolean on input events and is off the command critical path except for the strategy's later boolean read.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One listener per newly created tool terminal; cached foreground reuse does not register another listener, and disposal removes it.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Callbacks execute synchronously per input event with constant work; no queued async work or concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Listener ownership follows the cached terminal lifetime and is disposed once with terminal disposal; cache reuse does not duplicate registration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _registerInputListener is called only after terminal creation, cached terminals return before it, and Event.once(onDisposed) disposes the subscription.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Input event frequency varies with user/tool writes, but callback work is constant and output-heavy PTY traffic no longer invokes it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup or retention regression; listener cardinality and lifecycle remain bounded, with a cooler event source.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all seven changed files and complete diff pages. Traced PTY writes, idle waits, listener ownership, normal/recovery execution, shell detection, cache reuse, and concurrency. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame attribution.
